subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 7-year-old boy is evaluated for declining school performance, behavioral changes, and a progressive spastic gait. MRI shows symmetric demyelination of the cerebral white matter. Examination also shows hyperpigmentation and low serum cortisol with elevated ACTH, and plasma very-long-chain fatty acids are markedly elevated.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation_correct: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy is caused by a mutation in ABCD1, impairing peroxisomal beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids, which accumulate in the adrenal cortex, white matter, and testes. Boys present with progressive demyelination and adrenal insufficiency, and the disorder is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern.

explanation_incorrect.A: Zellweger syndrome is a defect of peroxisome biogenesis (PEX genes) with hypotonia, seizures, craniofacial dysmorphism, and early death rather than isolated adrenal and white matter disease.
explanation_incorrect.B: Refsum disease results from defective alpha-oxidation with phytanic acid accumulation and presents with retinitis pigmentosa, anosmia, hearing loss, ataxia, and peripheral neuropathy.
explanation_incorrect.C: Abetalipoproteinemia is a microsomal triglyceride transfer protein defect with fat malabsorption, acanthocytosis, and retinitis pigmentosa.
explanation_incorrect.E: Tay-Sachs disease is hexosaminidase A deficiency with developmental regression, macrocephaly, and a cherry-red macula.

educationalObjective: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy impairs peroxisomal beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids, causing demyelination and adrenal insufficiency.
